headline: High-risk default interaction: Devin’s autonomous workspace and Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side flows create dangerous write, exfiltration, and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, Slack, GitHub, and MCP content in an autonomous workspace, while Langflow can chain tools and agents through server-side flows. If Langflow outputs are fed into Devin via shared integrations or files, attacker-controlled flow content can steer Devin. The shared-channel pathway is plausible, though not proven by docs alone.
conditions: IF Langflow flow outputs are copied into Devin tasks or files without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF a shared integration passes Langflow text into Devin's workspace, Devin may treat it as instructions.
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff of Langflow outputs into Devin tasks.
Add a strict instruction/content delimiter in any shared file or ticket.
Require human review before Devin executes content originating from Langflow.
Use separate workspaces and separate integration channels for the two agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens in a cloud workspace, and Langflow stores per-flow credentials while reading uploaded files on a server filesystem. If both touch the same sensitive project data through shared integrations or files, either agent can expose secrets or intermediate outputs to the other’s broader network egress. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF the same secrets or sensitive files are available to both agents, leakage risk is present.
IF Langflow flows send uploaded content to external model providers, data can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared files and flow inputs.
Rotate any credentials used in either agent after shared handling.
Restrict Langflow flows to non-sensitive test data.
Separate network egress destinations for each agent.
Audit recent uploads and integration logs for sensitive content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files and execute shells, and Devin can modify git state while Langflow runs unsandboxed Python server-side by default. On a shared repo or workspace, concurrent writes can clobber files, corrupt branches, or overwrite flow state. The overlap is direct and dangerous in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or server filesystem, write conflicts can occur.
IF Langflow Python components mutate shared state while Devin edits the repo, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories to each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts.
Enable locking or serialization around shared resources.
Use read-only copies for analysis tasks.
Require manual merge review for any concurrent git changes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is autonomous and can act on GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion, while Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools in a flow. If Devin’s outputs are fed into Langflow or vice versa without verification, one agent can amplify the other’s mistakes into external actions such as commits or tickets. The default action-taking surfaces make this a high-blast-radius cascade.
conditions: IF Langflow consumes Devin-generated text as authoritative input, errors can cascade.
IF Devin acts on Langflow-produced facts without a verification step, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require structured outputs with explicit confidence and provenance fields.
Limit Devin to draft-only actions until reviewed.
Disable auto-execution of Langflow tool outputs.
Log and diff all agent-to-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs in a vendor-managed cloud workspace, while Langflow stores flow credentials and processes uploaded files on a server filesystem. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents, retention and residency controls must be aligned.
IF Langflow stores credentials or uploads longer than Devin's workspace retention, policy mismatch exists.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flows.
Document retention settings for both systems.
Delete uploaded files and flow artifacts after use.
Review residency and DPA terms before production use.
Use synthetic data for cross-agent testing.
